subject: Pathology
summary: Plasma proteins maintain oncotic pressure, transport substances, and mediate immune responses. Their loss or dysfunction leads to edema, hypoalbuminaemia, and impaired immunity, especially in infections common in low‑resource settings.

sections.p: Plasma proteins are soluble proteins in blood plasma, mainly albumin, globulins, and fibrinogen. Diagnosis focuses on serum protein electrophoresis and albumin concentration.

t.b: Low albumin suggests loss (renal, hepatic, GI) or decreased synthesis.
A spike indicates plasma cell dyscrasia or lymphoma.
High ratio points to nephrotic syndrome or glomerulonephritis.

sections.p: Severity is graded by albumin level and clinical edema. Staging of nephrotic syndrome follows proteinuria and hypoalbuminaemia thresholds.
Loss of plasma proteins occurs via kidneys, liver, gut, or skin. Infections and inflammatory states increase capillary permeability.
Patients develop generalized edema, ascites, pleural effusion, and fatigue. Infections may worsen due to impaired transport of antibodies.
Key tests assess protein loss, synthesis, and immune status.

t.b: Indicates protein loss or decreased synthesis.
May signal consumption or liver failure.

sections.p: Rapid weight gain, respiratory distress, or altered mental status suggest fluid overload or severe hypoalbuminaemia.
Treat underlying cause, replace albumin if needed, and support organ function.

t.b: Improves intravascular volume and reduces edema.
Reduce glomerular pressure and protein loss.
Increase calories and protein to aid synthesis.

sections.p: Monitor albumin, edema, and renal function. Prevent infections and malnutrition.
Hypoalbuminaemia can mimic heart failure or liver disease; differentiate by imaging and liver tests.

whenToSeekHelp: Signs of infection unresponsive to treatment

faq.q: Why does low albumin cause edema?
faq.a: Albumin maintains oncotic pressure; low levels allow fluid to leak into interstitial spaces.
Yes, sepsis increases capillary permeability and protein loss.
Only if hypoalbuminaemia is severe or symptomatic; otherwise treat the cause.

exam: Explain how hypoalbuminaemia leads to pulmonary edema in a patient with nephrotic syndrome.
